extraction_text: Arjuna spoke words in accordance with dharma and benefit, causing Brahmins to abandon heterodox lifestyles and live at home while observing dharma.
Arjuna advised the king to maintain firm resolve and rule the earth that had been cleared of enemies.
After hearing Arjuna's words, Nakula looked at the king who observed all dharma and began to speak.
Nakula described the king as a great wise man who subdues enemies, with broad chest, purplish-red complexion, strong arms, and measured speech that moves hearts.
Nakula explained that at Vishakayupa sacred ground, the gods lit many fires, showing that even gods follow the path of action.
Nakula stated that ancestors who give life to both heterodox and orthodox followers also engage in action, and extreme heterodox followers deny Vedic teachings.
Nakula explained that Brahmins who don't abandon Vedic teachings in any action reach heaven via the path of gods.
Nakula described four types of renouncers: household renouncers, blind renouncers, begging renouncers, and teacher renouncers.
Nakula explained that household life, when weighed against other three lifestyles, is superior according to wise men.
Nakula concluded that one who maintains livelihood is the true renouncer, while foolishly abandoning home for forest is not true renunciation.
Nakula described household life as serving parents, gods, and guests, containing the three fruits of dharma, benefit, and desire.
